correctness.rationale: For 0<μ<1 write a=1−μ. Linearized one-edge SIS matrices M12=aI+λA12 and M23=aI+λA23 yield P=M23 M12 on three nodes; independently expanded determinant det(P−I)=[(a−1)^2(a+1)−aλ²][(a−1)(a+1)^2−aλ²]. The second factor is strictly negative for a∈(0,1), λ≥0; the nonnegative irreducible P increases in λ and crosses Perron radius 1 exactly once at λ_temp²=μ²(2−μ)/(1−μ). The averaged adjacency matrix (A12+A23)/2 has radius 1/√2, giving λ_agg=μ√2 and λ_temp/λ_agg=sqrt((2−μ)/(2(1−μ)))>1. Two vertices cannot host distinct single-edge snapshots; every two distinct edges on three vertices share an endpoint and define this unique pattern. The threshold is formal when >1 (transmission probability cannot exceed one), and no exact finite-population stochastic extinction claim is made. Independent algebra checks determinant and ratio.
